designs.plain: A plain agent running as the signed-in user with a careful prompt
designs.abp: The same agent with an Agent Behaviour Policy: reach, mandate, gap, barriers
designs.abp_mxc_acs: The same policy with each row placed at the lowest layer that can enforce it: MXC, ACS, the tool, or a named acceptor

outcomes.named-hope: named gap row, barrier is an expectation
outcomes.mandate-hope: mandate states the rule, barrier is an expectation
outcomes.limits-hope: limits written, barrier is an expectation
outcomes.boundary-os: boundary enforced by the operating system via MXC
outcomes.boundary-if-written: a boundary once the business's rule is written into ACS, the tool or the system of record
outcomes.bounded-and-accepted: bounded where possible, residual accepted by a named person

scenarios.scenario: Coding agent rewrites the production server config to finish faster
scenarios.how: MXC readonlyPaths on the config path

scenarios.scenario: Coding agent reads SSH keys or Documents
Generated code posts the repository to an unknown host
Coding agent force-pushes to main on the allowed code host
scenarios.how: Same address and port to MXC; rule in an ACS pre_tool_call policy or the code host's branch protection

scenarios.scenario: Mailbox agent removes a payables label from forty messages
scenarios.how: MXC sees an allowed TLS connection; ACS or the tool must encode protected labels; connector twin restores labels, not consequences

scenarios.scenario: Agent replies in a person's voice to a real external contact
scenarios.how: An external-recipient rule does not catch it; no send tool, or a second reader gating drafts at the harness

scenarios.scenario: Support agent issues fifty refunds in an afternoon
scenarios.how: MXC cannot count; limit in the refund tool or an ACS policy given the session history

scenarios.scenario: A real customer's compromised mailbox asks for a new address and refunds
scenarios.how: Every call is inside the mandate; confirmation link, per-customer cap, named owner and interval
